nodehealth.s.notLinux: This node is not running on Linux ({{platform}}), so there are no cgroup files to read.
nodehealth.s.noCgroup: There is no cgroup at {{root}}: no cgroup v2 ({{why}}) and no cgroup v1 memory or cpuacct controller.
nodehealth.s.cpuUnreadable: The container's CPU time cannot be read: {{source}} — {{why}}.
nodehealth.s.cpuOnce: The container's CPU time could be read once and not a second time: {{why}}.
nodehealth.s.cpuQuota: The container may use {{vcpus}} vCPU ({{version}}, {{file}}), and the percentage is of that.
nodehealth.s.cpuNoFile: This cgroup ({{version}}) has no {{file}}, so it has no CPU quota of its own; the percentage is of the {{cpus}} CPU(s) node reports available (os.availableParallelism()).
nodehealth.s.cpuUnlimited: No CPU quota ({{version}}, {{file}} says none): the container may use every CPU the host gives it, and the percentage is of the {{cpus}} CPU(s) node reports available (os.availableParallelism()).
nodehealth.s.noThrottling: The cgroup has no throttling counters: with no quota there is nothing to throttle against.
nodehealth.s.noV1Memory: This cgroup v1 host has no memory controller for this process.
nodehealth.s.memoryUnreadable: The container's memory cannot be read: {{source}} — {{why}}.
nodehealth.s.memoryNoFile: This cgroup ({{version}}) has no {{file}}, so it has no memory limit of its own and there is no percentage to give.
nodehealth.s.memoryUnlimited: No memory limit ({{version}}, {{file}} says none), so there is no percentage to give.
nodehealth.s.memoryStat: {{anon}} is the processes' own memory; {{file}} is page cache the kernel reclaims under pressure before it kills anything.
nodehealth.s.memoryNoStat: memory.stat cannot be read, so what the memory is made of is not known.
nodehealth.s.ecsMemoryContainer: From the ECS agent (/task/stats), because the cgroup cannot be read here. The limit is the container's, as the agent reports it.
nodehealth.s.ecsMemoryTask: From the ECS agent (/task/stats), because the cgroup cannot be read here. The container has no limit of its own, so the limit is the ECS TASK's, {{mib}} MiB.
nodehealth.s.ecsMemoryNone: From the ECS agent (/task/stats), because the cgroup cannot be read here. There is no limit to measure against.
nodehealth.s.ecsTotalOnly: The ECS agent reports the total only.
nodehealth.s.taskMemoryLimit: The container has no memory limit of its own (cgroup v{{version}}), so the limit is the ECS TASK's, {{mib}} MiB (/task Limits.Memory), and the percentage is of that.
nodehealth.s.ecsCpuTask: From the ECS agent (/task/stats), between its last two samples, because the cgroup cannot be read here; the percentage is of the ECS TASK's {{vcpus}} vCPU.
nodehealth.s.ecsCpuNone: From the ECS agent (/task/stats), between its last two samples, because the cgroup cannot be read here; the task names no CPU limit, so there is no percentage.
nodehealth.s.ecsNoThrottling: The ECS agent does not report throttling.
nodehealth.s.taskCpuLimit: The container has no CPU quota of its own (cgroup v{{version}}), so the percentage is of the ECS TASK's {{vcpus}} vCPU (/task Limits.CPU).
nodehealth.s.noVmRss: its status file has no VmRSS
nodehealth.s.threadProcessWide: a thread's resident size and CPU time are the whole process's, so they are on the front process's row (pid {{pid}}) and not repeated here
nodehealth.s.frontProcessWide: its resident size and CPU time are the whole process's, every worker thread's included; its heap figures are its main thread's
nodehealth.s.childNoMemory: it answered without its memory, so only its resident size is shown, from /proc
nodehealth.s.childNoAnswer: {{why}}, so only its resident size is shown, from /proc
nodehealth.s.debuggerSilent: it did not answer within {{ms}}ms (its memory preload, debugger_api_status.js, answers when it is installed)
nodehealth.s.threadUnanswered: {{why}}; a thread has no /proc entry of its own, so its heap cannot be read from outside it
nodehealth.s.debuggerNoPid: The protocol debugger's api process could not be asked for its pid: {{error}}.
nodehealth.s.totals: The request and hosted-surface workers are THREADS of the front process (#364), so their resident size and CPU time are the front process's own figures and are counted once, on its row. The resident total is the sum over the {{rss}} process(es) whose size could be read — the front process and the debugger's api child — so pages the two share (node's own code among them) are counted once for each and it can exceed the container's memory.current. The heap figures are the {{heap}} V8 isolate(s) that reported process.memoryUsage() themselves: the front process's main thread, each worker thread, and the child; a child process that did not answer in time is shown with its resident size from /proc and no heap, and a worker thread that did not is listed as unanswered, since a thread has no /proc entry of its own. Post-quantum signing and scrypt have had no processes of their own since #363: they run on libuv's thread pool, and their memory is counted in the process that asked.
nodehealth.s.ecsNotSet: ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4 is not set: this node is not an Amazon ECS task (it is not on Fargate or an ECS container instance), so there is no task metadata endpoint to cross-check the cgroup against.
nodehealth.s.ecsSilent: ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4 is set, but the task metadata endpoint did not answer within {{ms}}ms: {{why}}.
nodehealth.s.ecsPartial: Part of the endpoint did not answer: {{whys}}.
nodehealth.s.ecsPartialNoStats: Part of the endpoint did not answer: {{whys}}. There are no stats for this container in /task/stats.
nodehealth.s.ecsPartialNoStatsId: Part of the endpoint did not answer: {{whys}}. There are no stats for this container in /task/stats ({{dockerId}}).
nodehealth.s.ecsNoStats: There are no stats for this container in /task/stats.
nodehealth.s.ecsNoStatsId: There are no stats for this container in /task/stats ({{dockerId}}).
nodehealth.s.ecsText: The ECS agent's own figures for this container, as a cross-check of the cgroup: the agent samples on its own schedule, so they will not agree to the byte or the percent.
nodehealth.s.scope: These are the figures of the node {{node}} — its container — drawn by its front process, pid {{pid}}. Every node of a cluster is a container of its own, with its own figures.
nodehealth.s.machine: The machine this container runs on — on Fargate, the micro-VM; on a workstation, the whole workstation. NOT the container: its free memory and load say nothing about the container's limit.
nodehealth.s.clusterTotals: Over the {{count}} node(s) that are not gone and have a snapshot, stale ones included and marked. The limits are summed only when every node has one.
nodehealth.param.noCpuacct: there is no cgroup v1 cpuacct controller
